candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7: participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes; utilize resources to promote quality client care; practice and advocate for quality care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — quality improvement and data-driven systems improvement
candidate.educational_objective: Describe continuous quality improvement as an ongoing systematic process of setting goals, testing changes, measuring results, learning, and refining care processes.

options.A: End the improvement process once the organization proves that a minimum external standard has been met for the current review period.
options.B: Focus primarily on identifying the individual responsible after an adverse event instead of examining the processes that shaped performance.
options.C: Limit quality-improvement work to external accreditation surveys rather than integrating measurement and testing into routine operations.
options.D: Use an ongoing, systematic, data-driven process that sets goals, tests changes, measures performance, learns from results, and continues improving care processes.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ EvidenceNOW describes quality improvement as a systematic, data-driven process for managing change. It recommends setting improvement goals, identifying and testing changes, selecting measures, collecting and reviewing data regularly, comparing results with goals/benchmarks, and acting on the data. D best represents continuous quality improvement.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Continuous quality improvement is a systematic data-driven process that repeatedly measures performance, tests changes, evaluates results, and acts on learning to improve care processes.
